chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Yazid ibn Ishaq, from Harun ibn Hamzah al-Ghanawi, from Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about salat (prayer) in a ship. He said: If it is heavily loaded, such that when you stand in it, it does not move, then perform salat standing; but if it is light and tilts, then perform salat sitting.

key_terms.السَّفِينَةِ: ship or boat, the place where the prayer is performed
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer), the ritual prayer being discussed
key_terms.تَتَحَرَّكْ: move or shift, referring to instability while standing
key_terms.تَكَفَّأُ: tilts or inclines, describing the rocking of a light vessel
key_terms.ثَقِيلَةً: heavy, indicating a condition of steadiness
key_terms.قَائِمًا: standing, the required posture when possible
key_terms.قَاعِدًا: sitting, the permitted posture when standing is not feasible
key_terms.مُحَمَّلَةً: loaded, carrying weight so as to be more stable

ai.seo_question: How should salat (prayer) be performed in a ship according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for performing salat (prayer) in a ship based on practical stability. If the vessel is stable enough for standing, one should pray standing; if it is unstable and liable to tilt, one should pray sitting.
